ct_title: Counterpoint checker — Fux’s first and second species
ct_intro: Type or draw the voices, listen to the result and see the rules point out each problem.
ct_entry_help: Notes separated by spaces: letter, accidental (# or b) and octave; C4 is middle C; r is a rest (only at the start of 2nd species). In 2nd species, two notes per cantus firmus note, except the last. Each added voice is checked against the cantus firmus, and the added voices against each other for parallels.
ct_roll_help: Click or drag in a column to place or move the selected voice’s note; clicking near another voice’s note selects that voice. Red rings are errors, amber ones warnings. Numbers below: the selected voice’s intervals with the cantus firmus.
ct_lily_help_before: The code uses absolute pitches and 2/2, and turns 1st species into whole notes and 2nd species into half notes. The
ct_lily_help_after: block makes LilyPond write a MIDI file too.

manifesto_p8: B.E.M presents itself not as discourse but as method. Musical excellence is not occasional. It is the product of conscious, continuous and directed work.
manifesto_p7: Solfège · Music Reading · Transcription · Improvisation · Classical Harmony · Analytical Harmony · Music Appreciation · Technique · Bibliography · Repertoire.
manifesto_p6: Musical learning happens in relation to others. We bring listening, performing and creating together as inseparable. Music is not an escape from reality, but a way to interpret and transform it. We recognise the privilege of living meaningfully through music, and with it, responsibility and gratitude.
manifesto_p5: Musicians take charge of their own development, working in constant cycles of planning, execution, observation and correction, with the help of tools such as recordings and a practice journal.
manifesto_p4: Growth on an instrument demands continuity. The image of the "down escalator" expresses the constant effort needed to keep and improve technique. We stand for daily practice, organised in cycles of focus and rest, recognising the role of rest in consolidating learning and in caring for the musician’s body. The B.E.M musician does not depend on passing motivation, but on organisation and clarity of method.
manifesto_p3: Musical practice is a field of decisions. Repetition alone does not lead to excellence, only to fixed patterns, right or wrong. So we hold that there is no neutral practice. Study must be guided by clear goals, aimed at solving specific problems, joining technique and musical intent.
manifesto_p2: We refuse the idea of music as something transcendent or autonomous. We will never make Music an empty goddess. It does not exist outside human making; it is made through intention and conscious action on sound. Without work, there is no music. Without awareness, there is no meaning. Practice without reflection reduces music-making to empty automatism.
manifesto_p1: We reject the idea of talent as predestination. The notion of a "gift" hides the work: it ignores the historical, social and material conditions that shape musical growth. Musical practice is shaped by context, access, teaching and the quality of study. Excellence is not innate; it is built.
manifesto_p0a: B.E.M affirms music as a process of intellectual and acoustic work, in which a person, through instruments and technical means, transforms sound and, at the same time, transforms themselves and the world they live in.
manifesto_p0b: Our goal is direct: to play well, understanding that musical excellence is the result of a continuous, conscious and historically situated process.
